content.title: Authenticate as standard_user from the documented login page
content.test_md_blob:
# Authenticate as standard_user from the documented login page

> Prove a valid full-access credential establishes an authenticated session and reaches the appropriate standard banking experience.

## Step 1 @verifies ac-1

Open https://qaplayground.com/bank/login in a browser, store the visible unauthenticated login page as baseline_login_state, then assert the browser URL is exactly https://qaplayground.com/bank/login.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-2, ac-3, ac-4, ac-5, ac-6, ac-7, ac-8

On the Bank Demo login page and its visible Test credentials section, enter username standard_user and password bank_sauce, use the password visibility control to reveal and then re-hide the entered password, and inspect the surrounding login controls, then assert the page shows a username field, a password field that masked the entered password before reveal, a visibility control that changes only the password visibility and not the typed value, a Remember me checkbox, a clearly labeled Sign In control, a Forgot password entry point, and credential rows for standard_user, locked_user, frozen_user, overdraft_user, slow_user, error_user, and admin_user.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-14, ac-17

Submit the standard_user credentials from the login page, then assert the unauthenticated login surface is replaced by an authenticated banking experience that corresponds to the standard user's normal/full-access view.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - baseline: true
    objective: Open https://qaplayground.com/bank/login in a browser, store the visible unauthenticated login page as baseline_login_state, then assert the browser URL is exactly https://qaplayground.com/bank/login.
    step: 1
    verifies:
      - ac-1
  - objective: On the Bank Demo login page and its visible Test credentials section, enter username standard_user and password bank_sauce, use the password visibility control to reveal and then re-hide the entered password, and inspect the surrounding login controls, then assert the page shows a username field, a password field that masked the entered password before reveal, a visibility control that changes only the password visibility and not the typed value, a Remember me checkbox, a clearly labeled Sign In control, a Forgot password entry point, and credential rows for standard_user, locked_user, frozen_user, overdraft_user, slow_user, error_user, and admin_user.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-2
      - ac-3
      - ac-4
      - ac-5
      - ac-6
      - ac-7
      - ac-8
  - check:
      baseline: unauthenticated login state
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: state-transition
      operand: authenticated session
      operator: equals
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-14
    objective: Submit the standard_user credentials from the login page, then assert the unauthenticated login surface is replaced by an authenticated banking experience that corresponds to the standard user's normal/full-access view.
    step: 3
    verifies:
      - ac-14
      - ac-17
scenario: Sign in successfully as standard_user
title: Authenticate as standard_user from the documented login page

content.title: Operate the login page through accessible names and keyboard input

check.operand: Remember me, Sign In, and Forgot password controls are keyboard operable

content.test_md_blob:
# Operate the login page through accessible names and keyboard input

> Prove the username and password fields expose accessible names, the password visibility control has an understandable accessible name, and Remember me, Sign In, and Forgot password are keyboard operable.

## Step 1

Open https://qaplayground.com/bank/login in a browser.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-9

Inspect the username and password fields on the Bank Demo login page through the browser's accessibility information, then assert each field exposes an accessible label or equivalent accessible name.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-10

Inspect the password visibility control through the browser's accessibility information, then assert it exposes an understandable accessible name.

## Step 4 @verifies ac-11

Using keyboard-only interaction on the Bank Demo login page, move to the Remember me checkbox and toggle it, then assert the checkbox state changes in response to the keyboard input.

## Step 5 @verifies ac-11

Using keyboard-only interaction on the Bank Demo login page, activate the Forgot password entry point, then assert it opens a forgot-password destination or recovery flow.

## Step 6 @verifies ac-11

Return to the Bank Demo login page, enter username standard_user and password bank_sauce, activate Sign In from the keyboard, then assert the authenticated banking experience opens from the keyboard-triggered submission.

judgements.rationale: [self_critique] The oracle directly proves the standard-user boundary by capturing the unauthenticated baseline and asserting an authenticated landing, while the control-inspection step proves the login-surface promises without broadening into undocumented dashboard details beyond a normal/full-access authenticated experience.

[self_critique] The negative technique fits because the promise is denial of access plus visible failure; the proving step now explicitly claims both ac-13 and ac-19. I used owner-approved placeholders for the invalid credentials because the corpus names only valid fixture values.

[self_critique] The locked-user test uses the correct security/negative technique and its oracle proves the important risk: no normal active session is granted. The proving step explicitly claims both the blocked-access and clear-outcome criteria without assuming any undocumented lock-message wording.

[self_critique] The admin-user test fits the auth-plus-role boundary and proves both session establishment and role-specific landing. The assert is intentionally limited to an authenticated administrative view with distinguishable admin information or controls, because the PRD does not name exact labels or pages.

[self_critique] The slow-user test splits the in-progress loading promise from the final resolution promise so the oracle proves progress separately from completion. The loading-state step now explicitly claims ac-20, and the baseline is captured before the completion action that proves ac-21.

[self_critique] The accessibility test uses browser-observable accessibility information and keyboard-only interactions, which fit the promised surface. Each operability proof asserts an outcome of the keyboard action rather than mere focus movement, reducing the risk of a false positive from superficial interaction.
